source_name: Google Trends (Brazil, Web Search, All categories)
source_published_at: weekly series to 2026-11-01 (last week partial, excluded)
universe_and_method: Google Trends relative search interest (0-100 within one export, peak = 100); weekly; captured per trends-method-v2.md; facts compare weeks inside the same export only; repeat exports differ by up to 5 index points (sampling)
observed_fact: In every year 2022-2026 the maximum week of 'chocolate' and of all five Set B2 brand terms is the week that starts seven days before Easter Sunday (2022-04-10, 2023-04-02, 2024-03-24, 2025-04-13, 2026-03-29). For 'chocolate' the Easter week is 2.3x the median week; the Christmas window maximum is 0.62-0.65 of the following Easter peak.
hypothesis: Shopper attention to chocolate in Brazil concentrates in the five weeks before Easter, with Christmas as a secondary season; brand search peaks coincide with the category peak.
alternative_explanations: Relative index, not sales; Easter-week searches include gifting and recipes, not only purchase; Trends sampling of up to 5 points.
independent_corroboration: FGV IBRE Easter basket release (SIG-CHOC-002) and Abicab Easter production figures in the Pulse public evidence (abicab-chocolate-producao-brasil-2025-pascoa-2026) are independent of search data.
decision_rationale: Proposed: accept as a consolidated seasonal baseline fact (two independent source families). Use: the Easter window E-4..E is the comparison frame for every later year.

universe_and_method: Google Trends relative search interest (0-100 within one export, peak = 100); weekly; captured per trends-method-v2.md; facts compare weeks inside the same export only; repeat exports differ by up to 5 index points (sampling)
observed_fact: Inside GT-CHOC-B2-5Y, the Christmas-window maximum relative to the following Easter peak is 0.71-0.90 for Lindt, 0.21-0.26 for Ferrero Rocher, 0.28-0.38 for the Nestlé union, 0.28 for the Garoto union and 0.15-0.19 for Lacta.
hypothesis: Lindt has a two-season search profile (Christmas nearly as strong as Easter); Lacta, Garoto and Nestlé are Easter-driven; Ferrero Rocher sits between.
alternative_explanations: Lindt's Christmas searches include panettone and gift queries ('panettone lindt' among Google's rising related queries), so part of the Christmas profile is not chocolate bars or bonbons; brand campaigns; store-locator searches for Lindt's own shops.
independent_corroboration: None in the kit yet; retail Christmas assortment or sell-out data would be needed.
decision_rationale: Proposed: preliminary; keep as a hypothesis for the Christmas 2026 observation window (weeks of 2026-11-29 to 2026-12-20).

source_name: Google Trends (Brazil, Web Search, All categories)
source_published_at: weekly series to 2026-11-01 (last week partial, excluded)
universe_and_method: Google Trends relative search interest (0-100 within one export, peak = 100); weekly; captured per trends-method-v2.md; facts compare weeks inside the same export only; repeat exports differ by up to 5 index points (sampling)
observed_fact: Easter-week index inside GT-CHOC-B2-5Y, 2022 to 2026: Lindt 38, 47, 54, 61, 62; Garoto union 23, 26, 30, 32, 36; Lacta 83, 91, 62, 62, 66; Ferrero Rocher 76, 100, 75, 68, 66; Nestlé union 30, 31, 28, 26, 31. Values are comparable inside this one export.
hypothesis: Easter search attention has shifted over five years from Lacta and Ferrero Rocher toward Lindt and toward chocolate-qualified Garoto searches, consistent with premiumisation at the top and value-seeking at the bottom.
alternative_explanations: Lindt's physical store expansion and gift occasions raise brand searches without raising chocolate purchases; the Garoto union counts product-qualified queries whose growth may reflect new launches or price searches; Lacta's 2022-2023 peaks may include campaign effects (Felipe Neto queries appear among rising related queries); sampling noise up to 5 points; relative index, not share.
independent_corroboration: Pulse public evidence niq-polarization-brazil (NIQ polarisation of premium and value) and kantar-chocolate-brasil-volume-q1-2025 (volume decline) point the same way but are not brand-level; no sell-out by brand in the kit.
decision_rationale: Proposed: preliminary, flagged as the main candidate shopper-side signal of the pilot; requires brand-level sell-out or panel corroboration before it is called a trend.

observed_fact: Easter-week index of 'chocolate' inside GT-CHOC-A-5Y: 93 (2022), 100 (2023), 90 (2024), 86 (2025), 87 (2026); median week 39 across the five years.
hypothesis: Easter-week search interest for the category term has been slightly lower since 2023 while the off-season level is stable.
alternative_explanations: Differences of 4-14 points are close to the 5-point sampling band; Easter dates move (late March in 2024 and 2026), which shifts school holidays and payday timing relative to the peak; search habits migrate to apps and assistants; the bare term 'chocolate' includes recipes and non-purchase intent.
independent_corroboration: Kantar Q1 2025 volume decline (Pulse evidence kantar-chocolate-brasil-volume-q1-2025) is a different measure and period.
decision_rationale: Proposed: context_only; too close to sampling noise to carry a decision.
